topicName: Azure DevOps Pipelines and GitHub Actions Integration
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Tutorial: Integrating Azure DevOps Pipelines with GitHub Actions"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Modern enterprise applications often leverage multiple platforms for source control and continuous integration. Organizations frequently use GitHub for developer workflows while maintaining enterprise deployments and governance in Azure DevOps. This tutorial demonstrates how to seamlessly integrate GitHub Actions with Azure DevOps Pipelines to bridge both ecosystems."},{"order":3,"type":"heading","text":"Prerequisites and Setup"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"An active Microsoft Azure subscription."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"An Azure DevOps organization and project with permissions to manage Service Connections."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"A GitHub repository containing your application source code."},{"order":7,"type":"heading","text":"Step 1: Authenticating GitHub Actions to Azure"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"To allow GitHub Actions to securely deploy resources to Azure without storing sensitive credentials in your repository, configure OpenID Connect (OIDC) or create a Service Principal using the Azure CLI."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"az ad sp create-for-rbac --name "myGitHubActionSP" --role contributor --scopes /subscriptions/YOUR_SUBSCRIPTION_ID --json-auth"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Copy the JSON output from the command above and add it as a secret named AZURE_CREDENTIALS in your GitHub repository settings under Secrets and variables -> Actions."},{"order":11,"type":"heading","text":"Step 2: Creating the GitHub Actions Workflow"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"Create a workflow file named .github/workflows/deploy.yml in your repository. This workflow will build your application and trigger an Azure DevOps pipeline via the Azure DevOps REST API once the build succeeds."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"name: Build and Trigger Azure DevOps

on:
  push:
    branches: [ "main" ]

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    
    - name: Azure Login
      uses: azure/login@v2
      with:
        creds: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}
        
    - name: Trigger Azure DevOps Pipeline
      run: |
        curl -X POST \
        -u ":YOUR_ADO_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN" \
        -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
        -d '{"definition": {"id": 1}, "sourceBranch": "refs/heads/main"}' \
        "https://dev.azure.com/YOUR_ORG/YOUR_PROJECT/_apis/build/builds?api-version=7.0""},{"order":14,"type":"heading","text":"Step 3: Configuring the Azure DevOps Pipeline"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"In your Azure DevOps project, create a YAML-based pipeline named azure-pipelines.yml that consumes artifacts or simply executes downstream deployment tasks upon being triggered."},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"trigger:
- none

pool:
  vmImage: 'ubuntu-latest'

steps:
- script: echo "Pipeline triggered successfully from GitHub Actions!"
  displayName: 'Run Deployment Task'"},{"order":17,"type":"heading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"By integrating GitHub Actions with Azure DevOps Pipelines, you harness the collaborative development speed of GitHub alongside the robust enterprise deployment governance of Microsoft Azure and Azure DevOps."}]
